version: Effort rules v17: independent monotone effort bands, descriptive near-even metadata and score-based stopping across allocations

The second experiment requires a changed split and never forces a direction or degree of balance

notes: The previous v16 source and downloads are frozen on archive/pre-effort-rules-v16 at69f2bb4906a6d6c85442686180e49dc6a0800291. Historical archives, versioned ZIPs and validation reports are preserved.

Every task now uses only its own weight:1–24 Minimum effort,25–66 Steady effort,67–98 Intense effort. Near-even remains max-minus-min at most10percentage points, but only labels the weight distribution. It never overrides an effort band or selects special criticism. Positive1–98 weights, total100 and linked-pair confirmation remain intact.

All4851 legal positive integer splits are checked in every card position for contextual invariance, own-share monotonicity and valid one-point transfers. Boundary tests cover24/25,66/67 and exact40/30/30→40/31/29; the raised31share remains medium. Uneven50/25/25 also naturally produces three medium responses.

The score-based closing observation appears for all allocations. Its marks reflect actual nonlow tasks: neglected low-effort tasks stay unticked. Every run shows checking rewards, collecting marks and packing up without claiming all three criteria are met when effort is unevenly neglected. Visible-time pausing and actual manual observation remain.

Medium task actions and fresh criterion-based replies now depend on medium effort, including uneven allocations, rather than a near-even override. Teacher questions, neglected task names and coverage findings use actual bands. Third-result dialogue says what is prioritized this time without falsely assuming it already was the priority. Comparison summaries distinguish actual shifts from unchanged effort patterns.

Dialogue checks cover all20trios,13200 complete cross-level scenario paths and4320 purpose/history paths with both final judgments. These representative paths include uneven all-medium splits and the24/25 boundary; no repeated dialogue lines or emojis are found. Replay remains deterministic.

Production-browser regressions exercise40/30/30→40/31/29→50/25/25 with identical medium effort and no false change claim;67/25/8→66/25/9→66/24/10 with accurate bands and partial ticks; and70/20/10→34/33/33→10/70/20 with true comparison changes and the final theory endpoint. A320px normal-motion route checks the universal stopping observation.

Existing production checks retain the task attention cue, optional editable examples, manual confirmation, three actual trial records, both final judgments and1366/768/390/320px comparison layouts. The earlier43/29/28→34/33/33→28/43/29 example now correctly remains medium across all records under the approved bands.

Partner-host checks verify opening names, selected-trio handoff, scene IDs, actual copied runs, once-only completion, nullable compared pairs, final decision context, custom renderer replacement, hidden-time pauses, real-time cues and sound. Final scene callbacks stay at theory.reveal and never invoke Design Lab.

All four final builds and all five latest ZIPs pass. CRC and SHA-256 checks establish that packaged HTML matches the final builds and current manifest. Actual packaged standalone Levels1/2/3 and the connected game pass offline routes; the review ZIP contains standalone Level3 and connected Levels1–3 from those same builds.

This release implements the approved underlying-rule step only. The existing aim selector, three required attempts, final judgment and inline guide remain pending the separately discussed player-path redesign. Level1/2 gameplay and the partner’s authored animation scripts are unchanged. Functional checks do not establish measured learning effectiveness or classroom hosting capacity.
